title.zh: 卷44 列傳第9 滕穆王瓚 道悼王靜 蔡王智積
title.en: Volume 44 Biographies 9: Teng Mu Wangzan, Daodao Wangjing, Caiwang Zhiji
title.raw: 卷44 列傳第9 滕穆王瓚 道悼王靜 蔡王智積 Volume 44 Biographies 9: Teng Mu Wangzan, Daodao Wangjing, Caiwang Zhiji

sentences.zh: 隋書卷四十四列傳第九

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume Forty-Four, Biographies Nine
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 44, Biographies 9

sentences.zh: 滕穆王瓚嗣王綸

translations.literal: Teng the Mu Prince Zan; heir Wang Lun
translations.idiomatic: Prince Teng the Mu, Zan; His Heir Wang Lun

sentences.zh: 膝穆王瓚，字恆生，一名慧，高祖母弟也。

translations.literal: Teng the Mu Prince Zan, styled Hengsheng, also named Hui, was a younger cousin on Empress Gao's side.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Teng the Mu, Zan, styled Hengsheng and also known as Hui, was a maternal cousin of Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 周世以太祖軍功封竟陵郡公，尚武帝妹順陽公主，自右中侍上士遷禦伯中大夫。

translations.literal: In the Zhou era, because of the Grand Duke's military achievements he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jingling Commandery, married Emperor Wu's younger sister Princess Shunyang, and rose from Right Palace Attendant Superior Gentleman to Imperial Chamberlain Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: During the Northern Zhou, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jingling for the Grand Duke's military service, married Emperor Wu's younger sister Princess Shunyang, and advanced from Right Palace Attendant to Imperial Chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，改為納言，授儀同。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, he was changed to Director of Discourse and granted Palace Attendant Companion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Baoding (564), he was appointed Director of Discourse and granted the rank of Palace Attendant Companion.

sentences.zh: 瓚貴公子，又尚公主，美姿儀，好書愛士，甚有令名於當世，時人號曰楊三郎。

translations.literal: Zan was a nobleman's son and had also married a princess; handsome in bearing, fond of books and cherishing scholars, he had a very fine reputation in his age, and people of the time called him Yang the Third Lord.
translations.idiomatic: As a prince of the blood who had married an imperial princess, Zan was striking in appearance, devoted to books, and generous to men of talent. He enjoyed great renown in his day, and contemporaries called him Yang the Third.

sentences.zh: 武帝甚親愛之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was very intimate with and fond of him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu held him in exceptional affection.

sentences.zh: 平齊之役，諸王鹹從，留瓚居守，帝謂之曰：「六府事殷，一以相付。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Qi, all the princes followed along; Zan was left to remain and guard, and the Emperor said to him: 'The Six Offices' affairs are pressing—I entrust them all to you.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign to conquer Qi began, all the princes went with the army, but Zan was left behind to hold the capital. The emperor told him, "The Six Offices are overwhelmed with business; I leave everything in your hands.

sentences.zh: 朕將遂事東方，無西顧之憂矣。

translations.literal: I shall complete the affair in the east and have no worry of looking back to the west.
translations.idiomatic: I am going east to finish the campaign, and I shall have no need to glance back over my shoulder toward the west.

sentences.zh: 」其見親信如此。

translations.literal: ' Thus was he seen to be trusted and favored.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the depth of trust placed in him.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，遷吏部中大夫，加上儀同。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan acceded, he was transferred to Grand Master of the Ministry of Personnel and given Senior Palace Attendant Companion.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Zan was promoted to Grand Master in the Ministry of Personnel and granted the rank of Senior Palace Attendant Companion.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝崩，高祖入禁中，將總朝政，令廢太子勇召之，欲有計議。

translations.literal: Before long the Emperor died; Gaozu entered the inner palace, was about to take overall control of court affairs, ordered the deposed Crown Prince Yong summoned, and wished to have plans discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor died. Gaozu entered the inner palace to assume control of the government, summoned the deposed Crown Prince Yong, and intended to consult with him on strategy.

sentences.zh: 瓚素與高祖不協，聞召不從，曰：「作隋國公恐不能保，何乃更為族滅事邪？

translations.literal: Zan had long been at odds with Gaozu; hearing the summons he did not obey and said: 'Being made Duke of Sui probably cannot be preserved—why then go further and do a thing that exterminates the clan?
translations.idiomatic: Zan had long been on bad terms with Gaozu. When he heard the summons, he refused to come and said, "Even as Duke of Sui you may not be able to keep your position—why press on toward something that will destroy the whole clan?

sentences.zh: 」高祖作相，遷大將軍。

translations.literal: ' When Gaozu became Chancellor, he was transferred to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: " After Gaozu became chancellor, Zan was appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 尋拜大宗伯，典修禮律。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Director of Ritual and supervised the compilation of ritual and penal codes.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Director of Ritual and put in charge of revising the ritual and penal codes.

sentences.zh: 進位上柱國、邵國公。

translations.literal: He advanced in rank to Senior Pillar of State and Duke of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Senior Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Shao.

sentences.zh: 瓚見高祖執政，群情未一，恐為家禍，陰有圖高祖之計，高祖每優容之。

translations.literal: Zan saw Gaozu holding power while popular sentiment was not united, feared a family disaster, and secretly had plans to plot against Gaozu; Gaozu each time treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Gaozu in power while opinion in the realm remained divided, Zan feared disaster for his own house and secretly plotted against him, yet Gaozu repeatedly showed him leniency.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，立為滕王。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, he was established as Prince of Teng.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Zan was created Prince of Teng.

sentences.zh: 後拜雍州牧。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 上數與同坐，呼為阿三。

translations.literal: The Emperor several times sat with him together and called him Little Third.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often sat with him as an equal and called him "Little Third."

sentences.zh: 後坐事去牧，以王就第。

translations.literal: Later, because of an affair, he was removed from the governorship and, as a prince, retired to his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was removed from office for an offense and returned to his princely residence.

sentences.zh: 瓚妃宇文氏，先時與獨孤皇后不平，及此鬱鬱不得志，陰有咒詛。

translations.literal: Zan's consort, of the Yuwen clan, had earlier been on bad terms with Empress Dugu; at this time, depressed and without achieving her aims, she secretly had curses and imprecations.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's consort, Lady Yuwen, had long been at odds with Empress Dugu. Now bitter and thwarted, she secretly practiced curses against the empress.

sentences.zh: 上命瓚出之，瓚不忍離絕，固請。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Zan to send her out; Zan could not bear to part from her and firmly pleaded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zan to divorce her, but Zan could not bear to cast her off and pleaded repeatedly to keep her.

sentences.zh: 上不得已，從之，宇文氏竟除屬籍。

translations.literal: The Emperor, having no alternative, followed this; the Yuwen clan was in the end removed from the register of kin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reluctantly agreed, but Lady Yuwen was ultimately struck from the imperial clan rolls.

sentences.zh: 瓚由是忤旨，恩禮更薄。

translations.literal: Zan thereby went against the imperial will, and favor and ceremony grew still thinner.
translations.idiomatic: From that point Zan fell out of favor, and the emperor's kindness toward him grew still colder.

sentences.zh: 開皇十一年，從幸栗園，暴薨，時年四十二。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kaihuang, accompanying the emperor on a visit to Chestnut Garden, he died suddenly; he was forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Kaihuang (591), while accompanying the emperor to Chestnut Garden, he died suddenly at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 人皆言其遇鴆以斃。

translations.literal: Everyone said that he encountered poisoned wine and died thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone said he had been killed by poisoned wine.

sentences.zh: 子綸嗣。

translations.literal: His son Lun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 綸字斌籀，性弘厚，美姿容，頗解鐘律。

translations.literal: Lun, styled Binzhou, was by nature magnanimous and generous, handsome in appearance, and rather understood bells and pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Lun, styled Binzhou, was openhearted and handsome and had considerable knowledge of music theory.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，封邵國公，邑八千戶。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shao with a fief of eight thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Lun was enfeoffed as Duke of Shao with a fief of eight thousand households.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜邵州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Governor of Shao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Governor of Shao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣納妃于梁，詔綸致禮焉，甚為梁人所敬。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Guang took a consort in Liang; an edict ordered Lun to convey the ceremonial gifts, and he was greatly respected by the people of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jin Guang took a bride from Liang, Lun was ordered to convey the betrothal gifts on his behalf and won great respect among the Liang court.

sentences.zh: 綸以穆王之故，當高祖之世，每不自安。

translations.literal: Because of the Mu Prince, during Gaozu's reign Lun was each time ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his father's disgrace as Prince Teng the Mu, Lun never felt secure throughout Gaozu's reign.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，尤被猜忌。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, he was especially subjected to suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang came to the throne, suspicion against him deepened still further.

sentences.zh: 綸憂懼不知所為，呼術者王琛而問之。

translations.literal: Lun, anxious and fearful, did not know what to do; he summoned the diviner Wang Chen and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Tormented by fear and uncertainty, Lun summoned the diviner Wang Chen to consult him.

sentences.zh: 琛答曰：「王相祿不凡。

translations.literal: Chen answered: 'Your princely physiognomy and emolument are not ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Chen replied, "Your Highness's countenance and fortune are no ordinary matter.

sentences.zh: 」乃因曰：「滕即騰也，此字足為善應。

translations.literal: ' He then took occasion to say: 'Teng is the same as soaring; this character is sufficient as a good omen.
translations.idiomatic: " He went on, "The character for Teng also means to soar—surely an auspicious sign for you.

sentences.zh: 」有沙門惠恩、崛多等，頗解占候，綸每與交通，常令此三人為度星法。

translations.literal: ' There were monks Hui'en, Jueduo, and others who were rather skilled in observing omens; Lun frequently associated with them and often had these three men perform star-measuring methods.
translations.idiomatic: " There were also the monks Hui'en and Jueduo, who were skilled in divination. Lun associated with them regularly and often had the three of them practice astrological prognostication.

sentences.zh: 有人告綸怨望咒詛，帝命黃門侍郎王弘窮治之。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Lun harbored resentment and cursed; the Emperor ordered Yellow Gate Attendant Wang Hong to investigate it to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Lun was nursing resentment and practicing curses. The emperor ordered Yellow Gate Attendant Wang Hong to investigate the case thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 弘見帝方怒，遂希旨奏綸厭蠱惡逆，坐當死。

translations.literal: Hong saw that the Emperor was just then angry and accordingly, to please the intent, memorialized that Lun had practiced malign sorcery and wicked rebellion and, by the statute, deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor's anger, Hong shaped his findings to please him and reported that Lun had practiced malign sorcery and treason, crimes punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 帝令公卿議其事，司徒楊素等曰：「綸希冀國災，以為身幸。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the nobles and ministers to discuss the matter; Minister of Education Yang Su and others said: 'Lun hoped for national disaster as his own personal good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the high ministers to deliberate. Minister of Education Yang Su and others said, "Lun has been praying for calamity to befall the state, treating national disaster as his personal opportunity.

sentences.zh: 原其懷惡之由，積自家世。

translations.literal: Tracing the origin of his harboring of evil, it accumulated from his own family for generations.
translations.idiomatic: The roots of his malice lie deep in his family's history.

sentences.zh: 惟皇運之始，四海同心，在於孔懷，彌須協力。

translations.literal: Only at the beginning of the imperial fortune, when the four seas were of one heart, among those of closest kin all the more must there be joined effort.
translations.idiomatic: At the dawn of a new dynasty, when the realm should stand united, those bound by the closest ties of kinship ought all the more to lend their strength together.

sentences.zh: 其先乃離阻大謀，棄同即異，父悖于前，子逆於後，非直覬覦朝廷，便是圖危社稷。

translations.literal: His forebears then obstructed great plans, abandoned unity and took to difference; the father was disloyal before, the son rebellious after—not merely coveting the court, but indeed plotting to endanger the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears obstructed great state designs, forsaking unity for division; the father rebelled in one generation and the son in the next. This is not mere ambition for the throne—it is a plot to bring down the dynasty itself.

sentences.zh: 為惡有狀，其罪莫大，刑茲無赦，抑有舊章，請依前律。

translations.literal: Doing evil has clear evidence; his crime is the greatest; punishment here admits no pardon—yet there are also old statutes; we request execution according to the prior code.
translations.idiomatic: The evidence of his crimes is clear, and no offense could be graver. The law allows no mercy here. We ask that he be sentenced under the established statutes.

sentences.zh: 」帝以公族不忍，除名為民，徙始安。

translations.literal: ' The Emperor, unable to bear this against a member of the imperial clan, struck his name from the rolls and made him a commoner, banishing him to Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: " Unable to bring himself to execute a kinsman, the emperor struck Lun from the rolls of nobility, reduced him to commoner status, and exiled him to Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 諸弟散徙邊郡。

translations.literal: His younger brothers were scattered and banished to frontier commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers were likewise dispersed to remote border commanderies.

sentences.zh: 大業七年，親征遼東，綸欲上表，請從軍自效，為郡司所遏。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daye, when the Emperor personally campaigned in Liaodong, Lun wished to submit a memorial requesting to follow the army and offer his service, but was blocked by the prefectural officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daye (611), when the emperor campaigned in person against Liaodong, Lun tried to submit a memorial offering to join the army and prove his loyalty, but the local officials prevented it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，複徙硃崖。

translations.literal: Before long he was again banished to Zhuya.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred again, this time to Zhuya.

sentences.zh: 及天下大亂，為賊林仕弘所逼，攜妻子竄于儋耳。

translations.literal: When the empire fell into great disorder, he was pressed by the bandit Lin Shihong, took wife and children, and fled to Dan'er.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire collapsed into chaos, he was harried by the rebel Lin Shihong and fled with his wife and children to Dan'er.

sentences.zh: 後歸大唐，為懷化縣公。

translations.literal: Later he returned to Great Tang and was made Duke of Huaihua County.
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted to the Tang and was enfeoffed as Duke of Huaihua County.

sentences.zh: 綸弟坦，字文籀，初封竟陵郡公，坐綸徙長沙。

translations.literal: Lun's younger brother Tan, styled Wenzhou, was at first enfeoffed as Duke of Jingling Commandery; implicated in Lun's case, he was banished to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's younger brother Tan, styled Wenzhou, had initially been enfeoffed as Duke of Jingling; implicated in Lun's case, he was exiled to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 坦弟猛，字武籀，徙衡山。

translations.literal: Tan's younger brother Meng, styled Wuzhou, was banished to Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's younger brother Meng, styled Wuzhou, was exiled to Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 猛弟溫，字明籀，初徙零陵。

translations.literal: Meng's younger brother Wen, styled Mingzhou, was at first banished to Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Meng's younger brother Wen, styled Mingzhou, was first exiled to Lingling.

sentences.zh: 溫好學，解屬文，既而作《零陵賦》以自寄，其辭哀思。

translations.literal: Wen loved learning and understood literary composition; afterward he wrote 'Rhapsody on Lingling' to express himself, and its language was mournful and longing.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was studious and skilled at composition. He later wrote "Rhapsody on Lingling" to give voice to his grief, and its language was full of sorrow.

sentences.zh: 帝見而怒之，轉徙南海。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw it and was angry; he was transferred in banishment to Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor read it, he flew into a rage and had Wen transferred to Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 溫弟詵，字弘籀，前亦徙零陵。

translations.literal: Wen's younger brother Shen, styled Hongzhou, had earlier also been banished to Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's younger brother Shen, styled Hongzhou, had earlier been exiled to Lingling as well.

sentences.zh: 帝以其修謹，襲封滕王，以奉穆王嗣。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because of his cultivated carefulness, had him succeed to the enfeoffment as Prince of Teng to maintain the Mu Prince's line.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his prudent and dutiful conduct, the emperor had him succeed as Prince of Teng to maintain the line of Prince Teng the Mu.

sentences.zh: 大業末，薨于江都。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he died at Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era he died at Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: ○道悼王靜

translations.literal: ○ Prince of Dao the Lamented, Jing
translations.idiomatic: ○ Prince of Dao the Lamented, Jing

sentences.zh: 道悼王靜，字賢籀，滕穆王瓚之子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Dao the Lamented, Jing, styled Xianzhou, was the son of Teng the Mu Prince Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Dao the Lamented, Jing, styled Xianzhou, was a son of Prince Teng the Mu, Zan.

sentences.zh: 出繼叔父嵩。

translations.literal: He went out to succeed his paternal uncle Song.
translations.idiomatic: He was given in adoption to succeed his uncle Song.

sentences.zh: 嵩在周代，以太祖軍功，賜爵興城公，早卒。

translations.literal: Song, in the Zhou era, because of the Grand Duke's military achievements, was granted the title Duke of Xingcheng and died early.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhou, Song had been granted the title Duke of Xingcheng for the Grand Duke's military service and died young.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐位，追封道王，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Dao with posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne, Song was posthumously created Prince of Dao with the temple name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 以靜襲焉。

translations.literal: Jing succeeded to this.
translations.idiomatic: Jing succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子，國除。

translations.literal: He died without sons, and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He died without heirs, and the princedom was abolished.

sentences.zh: ○衛昭王爽嗣王集

translations.literal: ○ Wei the Illustrious Prince Shuang; heir Wang Ji
translations.idiomatic: ○ Prince of Wei the Illustrious, Shuang; His Heir Wang Ji

sentences.zh: 衛昭王爽，字師仁，小字明達，高祖異母弟也。

translations.literal: Wei the Illustrious Prince Shuang, styled Shiren, childhood name Mingda, was Gaozu's younger brother by a different mother.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei the Illustrious, Shuang, styled Shiren and known in youth as Mingda, was Gaozu's younger half-brother.

sentences.zh: 周世，在繈褓中，以太祖軍功，封同安郡公。

translations.literal: In the Zhou era, while still in swaddling clothes, because of the Grand Duke's military achievements he was enfeoffed as Duke of Tong'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhou, while still an infant, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Tong'an for the Grand Duke's military service.

sentences.zh: 六歲而太祖崩，為獻皇后之所鞠養，由是高祖于諸弟中特寵愛之。

translations.literal: At six years the Grand Duke died; he was reared and nourished by Empress Xian, and thereby Gaozu among all his younger brothers especially favored and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was six the Grand Duke died, and Empress Xian raised him herself. For this reason Gaozu cherished him above all his other brothers.

sentences.zh: 十七為內史上士。

translations.literal: At seventeen he became Palace Secretariat Superior Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he was appointed Superior Gentleman in the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖執政，拜大將軍、秦州總管。

translations.literal: When Gaozu held power, he was appointed Grand General and Commander-in-Chief of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu assumed control of the government, Shuang was appointed Grand General and Commander-in-Chief of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 未之官，轉授蒲州刺史，進位柱國。

translations.literal: He did not take up the post; he was transferred and appointed Governor of Pu Prefecture and advanced to Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He never took up the Qin post and was instead appointed Governor of Pu Prefecture and promoted to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，立為衛王。

translations.literal: When the abdication was received, he was established as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Shuang was created Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 尋遷雍州牧，領左右將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Governor of Yong Province and concurrently led the Left and Right Generals.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Governor of Yong Province and placed in command of the Left and Right Guards.

sentences.zh: 俄遷右領軍大將軍，權領并州總管。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Grand General of the Right Army Guard and provisionally commanded Bing Province as Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made Grand General of the Right Army Guard and given provisional authority as Commander-in-Chief of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，進位上柱國，轉涼州總管。

translations.literal: After more than a year he advanced to Senior Pillar of State and was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was promoted to Senior Pillar of State and transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 爽美風儀，有器局，治甚有聲。

translations.literal: Shuang was handsome in bearing and had capacity and vision; his governance had a very fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang was distinguished in bearing, possessed breadth of vision, and governed with great renown.

sentences.zh: 其年，以爽為行軍元帥，步騎七萬以備胡。

translations.literal: That year, with Shuang as campaign commander-in-chief, seventy thousand foot and horse were sent to guard against the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shuang was made campaign commander-in-chief with seventy thousand infantry and cavalry to guard against the northern peoples.

sentences.zh: 出平涼，無虜而還。

translations.literal: He went out from Pingliang; there were no barbarians and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He marched out from Pingliang, found no enemy, and returned.

sentences.zh: 明年，大舉北伐，又為元帥。

translations.literal: The next year, on a great northern expedition, he again served as commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, on a major northern campaign, he again served as commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 河間王弘、豆盧勣、竇榮定、高熲、虞慶則等分道而進，俱受爽節度。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Hong, Doulu Ji, Dou Rongding, Gao Jiong, Yu Qingze, and others advanced by separate routes, all receiving Shuang's command and control.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hejian Hong, Doulu Ji, Dou Rongding, Gao Jiong, Yu Qingze, and others advanced on separate routes, all under Shuang's command.

sentences.zh: 爽親率李充節等四將出朔州，遇沙缽略可汗于白道，接戰，大破之，虜獲千餘人，驅馬牛羊巨萬。

translations.literal: Shuang personally led Li Chongjie and four other generals out from Shuozhou, encountered Shabolüe Qaghan on White Road, joined battle, and routed him greatly; captives numbered more than a thousand, and horses, cattle, and sheep driven off were in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang personally led Li Chongjie and three other generals out of Shuozhou, met Qaghan Shabolüe at White Road, and routed him decisively. They took more than a thousand prisoners and drove off tens of thousands of horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略可汗中重創而遁。

translations.literal: Shabolüe Qaghan was struck with a grave wound and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan Shabolüe himself was gravely wounded and fled.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，賜爽真食梁安縣千戶。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and granted Shuang a true fief of one thousand households in Liang'an County.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted and granted Shuang a permanent fief of one thousand households in Liang'an County.

sentences.zh: 六年，複為元帥，步騎十五萬，出合川。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again served as commander-in-chief with one hundred fifty thousand foot and horse, going out from Hechuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he again served as commander-in-chief at the head of one hundred fifty thousand troops, marching out from Hechuan.

sentences.zh: 突厥遁逃而返。

translations.literal: The Turks fled in escape and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks fled before him, and he returned without a major engagement.

sentences.zh: 明年，征為納言。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned to serve as Director of Discourse.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled to court as Director of Discourse.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚重之。

translations.literal: Gaozu greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu held him in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 未幾，爽寢疾，上使巫者薛榮宗視之，雲眾鬼為厲。

translations.literal: Before long Shuang took to his bed with illness; the Emperor sent the shaman Xue Rongzong to observe him, who said that many ghosts were causing his affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shuang fell gravely ill. The emperor sent the shaman Xue Rongzong to examine him, and Rongzong reported that a host of ghosts were tormenting him.

sentences.zh: 爽令左右驅逐之。

translations.literal: Shuang ordered his attendants to drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang ordered his attendants to drive the spirits away.

sentences.zh: 居數日，有鬼物來擊榮宗，榮宗走下階而斃。

translations.literal: After several days, ghostly things came and struck Rongzong; Rongzong went down the steps and died.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later ghostly beings attacked Rongzong; he stumbled down the steps and died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 其夜爽薨，時年二十五。

translations.literal: That night Shuang died; he was twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: That same night Shuang died at the age of twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Commandant and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 子集嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ji succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 集字文會，初封遂安王，尋襲封衛王。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Wenhui, was at first enfeoffed as Prince of Suian; soon he succeeded to the enfeoffment as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, styled Wenhui, was first created Prince of Suian and soon succeeded as Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時，諸侯王恩禮漸薄，猜防日甚。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yang's time, for the feudal princes favor and ceremony gradually grew thin, and suspicion and guard daily deepened.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang, princes of the blood received ever less honor and favor, while suspicion and surveillance grew daily sharper.

sentences.zh: 集憂懼不知所為，乃呼術者俞普明章醮以祈福助。

translations.literal: Ji, anxious and fearful, did not know what to do; he then summoned the technician Yu Puming to perform zhang jiao rites to seek blessing and aid.
translations.idiomatic: Consumed by anxiety and fear, Ji summoned the ritual specialist Yu Puming to perform Daoist rites of supplication for divine aid.

sentences.zh: 有人告集咒詛，憲司希旨，鍛成其獄，奏集惡逆，坐當死。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Ji cursed; the judicial office, to please the intent, forged the case to completion and memorialized that Ji had committed wicked rebellion and, by the statute, deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Ji was practicing curses. The judicial authorities shaped the case to please the throne, convicted him of treason, and recommended the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 天子下公卿議其事，楊素等曰：「集密懷左道，厭蠱君親，公然咒詛，無慚幽顯。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent the matter down to the nobles and ministers for discussion; Yang Su and others said: 'Ji secretly harbored the left path, practiced malign sorcery against ruler and kin, openly cursed and imprecated, without shame before the hidden and the manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the case to the high ministers for deliberation. Yang Su and others said, "Ji has secretly embraced heterodox arts, practiced malign sorcery against his sovereign and kin, and openly uttered curses without shame before Heaven or earth.

sentences.zh: 情滅人理，事悖先朝，是君父之罪人，非臣子之所赦，請論如律。

translations.literal: His sentiment extinguishes human reason, his affairs rebel against the former court—he is a criminal against ruler and father, not one whom subjects and sons may pardon; we request judgment according to the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: He has abandoned all human decency and violated the principles of the founding reign. He is a criminal against his sovereign and father, and no subject may excuse such conduct. We ask that he be sentenced under the law.

sentences.zh: 」時滕王綸坐與相連，帝不忍加誅，乃下詔曰：「綸、集以附萼之華，猶子之重，縻之好爵，匪由德進。

translations.literal: ' At that time Prince of Teng Lun was implicated and connected in the case; the Emperor could not bear to execute them and issued an edict saying: 'Lun and Ji, as the blossom attached to the calyx, bear the weight due a son of the imperial line—they were bound to fine ranks, not advanced by virtue.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Prince of Teng Lun was implicated in the same affair. Unable to bring himself to execute them, the emperor issued an edict: "Lun and Ji are like blossoms on the imperial stem, bearing the weight of princes of the blood. They were granted noble rank, yet not for any merit of their own.

sentences.zh: 正應與國升降，休戚是同，乃包藏妖禍，誕縱邪僻。

translations.literal: They ought properly to rise and fall with the state and share its joys and sorrows alike; yet they harbored demonic calamity and wantonly indulged wicked perversity.
translations.idiomatic: They ought to rise and fall with the dynasty and share its fortunes. Instead they harbored malign designs and gave free rein to wickedness.

sentences.zh: 在三之義，愛敬俱淪；

translations.literal: The obligations among the three—love and respect were both lost;
translations.idiomatic: The bonds of the three relationships—love and respect alike—have been utterly abandoned;

sentences.zh: 急難之情，孔懷頓滅。

translations.literal: the feeling in urgent hardship—close kinship suddenly extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: and the ties of kinship in times of crisis have been cast aside entirely.

sentences.zh: 公卿議既如此，覽以潸然。

translations.literal: The nobles' discussion being thus, on reading it tears flowed.
translations.idiomatic: When I read the ministers' recommendation, tears came to my eyes.

sentences.zh: 雖複王法無私，恩從義斷，但法隱公族，禮有親親。

translations.literal: Although the king's law knows no partiality and favor must yield to righteousness, yet the law makes allowance for the imperial clan and ritual has its cherishing of kin.
translations.idiomatic: Though the law knows no favoritism and affection must yield to justice, the statutes make allowance for the imperial clan, and ritual teaches us to cherish our kin.

sentences.zh: 致之極辟，情所未忍。

translations.literal: To bring them to extreme punishment—emotion could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: To put them to death is more than my heart can endure.

sentences.zh: 」於是除名為民，遠徙邊郡。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon their names were struck and they were made commoners, banished far to frontier commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore struck their names from the rolls, reduced them to commoner status, and exiled them to remote border commanderies.

sentences.zh: 遇天下大亂，不知所終。

translations.literal: When the empire fell into great disorder, no one knew their end.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire collapsed into chaos, no one knew what became of him.

sentences.zh: ○蔡王智積

translations.literal: ○ Prince of Cai Zhiji
translations.idiomatic: ○ Prince of Cai Zhiji

sentences.zh: 蔡王智積，高祖弟整之子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Cai Zhiji was the son of Gaozu's younger brother Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Cai Zhiji was the son of Gaozu's younger brother Zheng.

sentences.zh: 整周明帝時，以太祖軍功，賜爵陳留郡公。

translations.literal: Zheng, in Emperor Ming's time of Zhou, because of the Grand Duke's military achievements, was granted the title Duke of Chenliu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Ming of Zhou, Zheng was enfeoffed as Duke of Chenliu for the Grand Duke's military service.

sentences.zh: 尋授開府、車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Preceptorate and Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed to the Grand Preceptorate and made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從武帝平齊，至并州，力戰而死。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, he reached Bing Province and died fighting with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu in the conquest of Qi and died fighting fiercely at Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及高祖作相，贈柱國、大司徒、冀定瀛相懷衛趙貝八州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor, he was posthumously given Pillar of State, Grand Minister of Education, and Governor of the eight provinces Ji, Ding, Ying, Xiang, Huai, Wei, Zhao, and Bei.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became chancellor, Zheng was posthumously honored as Pillar of State and Grand Minister of Education and as Governor of Ji, Ding, Ying, Xiang, Huai, Wei, Zhao, and Bei.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，追封蔡王，諡曰景。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cai with posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne, Zheng was posthumously created Prince of Cai with the temple name Jing.

sentences.zh: 以智積襲焉。

translations.literal: Zhiji succeeded to this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiji succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 又封其弟智明為高陽郡公，智才為開封縣公。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Zhiming and Zhicai were also enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoyang Commandery and Duke of Kaifeng County respectively.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Zhiming and Zhicai were also enfeoffed, as Duke of Gaoyang and Duke of Kaifeng respectively.

sentences.zh: 尋拜智積為開府儀同三司，授同州刺史，儀衛資送甚盛。

translations.literal: Soon Zhiji was appointed Grand Preceptorate with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies and given the post of Governor of Tong Prefecture; ceremonial guards and supplies sent forth were very lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiji was soon appointed Grand Preceptorate with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies and made Governor of Tong Prefecture, with a splendid escort and lavish provisions for his journey.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以修謹聞，高祖善之。

translations.literal: Before long, because of his cultivated carefulness he became known, and Gaozu approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his prudent and dutiful conduct won notice, and Gaozu was pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 在州未嘗嬉戲遊獵，聽政之暇，端坐讀書，門無私謁。

translations.literal: In the prefecture he never played games or went hunting; in the leisure between hearing cases he sat upright reading books, and at his gate there were no private callers.
translations.idiomatic: As governor he never indulged in games or hunting. In the intervals between hearing cases he sat upright with a book, and no private visitors came to his gate.

sentences.zh: 有侍讀公孫尚儀，山東儒士，府佐楊君英、蕭德言，並有文學，時延於座，所設唯餅果，酒才三酌。

translations.literal: There were Reader-in-Waiting Gongsun Shangyi, a Shandong scholar, and prefectural aides Yang Junying and Xiao Deyan, all possessed of literary learning; he would from time to time invite them to his seat, and what was set out was only cakes and fruit, with wine no more than three rounds.
translations.idiomatic: His Reader-in-Waiting Gongsun Shangyi was a scholar from Shandong, and his aides Yang Junying and Xiao Deyan were men of letters. He would invite them to join him from time to time, but served only cakes and fruit, with no more than three rounds of wine.

sentences.zh: 家有女妓，唯年節嘉慶，奏於太妃之前，其簡靜如此。

translations.literal: His household had female performers, but only at New Year festivals and joyous celebrations would they perform before the Princess Dowager—such was his simplicity and quietness.
translations.idiomatic: He kept female musicians in his household, but they performed only at festivals and celebrations, and then only before the Princess Dowager. Such was the austerity of his ways.

sentences.zh: 昔高祖龍潛時，景王與高祖不睦，其太妃尉氏又與獨孤皇后不相諧，以是智積常懷危懼，每自貶損。

translations.literal: In former times, when Gaozu was still in obscurity, Prince Jing was on bad terms with Gaozu, and his Princess Dowager of the Yu clan was also not in harmony with Empress Dugu; for this reason Zhiji constantly harbored fear and danger and each time humbled himself.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days, when Gaozu was still rising to power, Prince Jing had been on bad terms with him, and Prince Jing's consort of the Yu clan had clashed with Empress Dugu. For this reason Zhiji lived in constant fear and continually humbled himself.

sentences.zh: 高祖知其若是，亦哀憐之。

translations.literal: Gaozu knew that he was thus and also pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu understood his situation and pitied him.

sentences.zh: 人或勸智積治產業者，智積曰：「昔平原露朽財帛，苦其多也。

translations.literal: Some urged Zhiji to manage estates and property; Zhiji said: 'In former times Pingyuan exposed rotting wealth and silk, vexed that there was so much.
translations.idiomatic: When someone urged Zhiji to build up his estates, he said, "Long ago the Prince of Pingyuan displayed his rotting stores of silk and gold, lamenting that he had too much.

sentences.zh: 吾幸無可露，何更營乎？

translations.literal: I am fortunate to have nothing to expose—why then go further and manage?
translations.idiomatic: I am fortunate to have nothing worth displaying—why should I accumulate more?

sentences.zh: 」有五男，止教讀《論語》、《孝經》而已，亦不令交通賓客。

translations.literal: ' He had five sons and taught them only to read the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety, and also did not allow them to associate with guests.
translations.idiomatic: " He had five sons and taught them only the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety, and would not let them cultivate connections with guests.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，智積答曰：「卿非知我者。

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, Zhiji answered: 'You are not one who knows me.
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, Zhiji replied, "You do not understand me at all.

sentences.zh: 」其意恐兒子有才能，以致禍也。

translations.literal: ' His meaning was that he feared his sons might have talent and thereby bring disaster.
translations.idiomatic: " His fear was that talented sons would bring disaster upon the family.

sentences.zh: 開皇二十年，征還京第，無他職任，闔門自守，非朝覲不出。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Kaihuang he was summoned back to his capital mansion, held no other office, kept his household closed and guarded, and did not go out except for court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Kaihuang he was recalled to the capital and given no further office. He kept his household closed and did not leave home except for required court audiences.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從駕江都，寢疾。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed the imperial carriage to Jiangdu and took to his bed with illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Daye he accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu and fell ill.

sentences.zh: 帝時疏薄骨肉，智積每不自安，及遇患，不呼醫。

translations.literal: The Emperor at that time was distant and thin toward his kin; Zhiji was each time ill at ease, and when he encountered illness he did not summon physicians.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had grown cold toward his kinsmen, and Zhiji had long lived in anxiety. When he fell ill, he did not call for a physician.

sentences.zh: 臨終，謂所親曰：「吾今日始知得保首領沒于地矣。

translations.literal: At the end, he said to those close to him: 'Today I finally know that I can preserve my head and be buried in the earth.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told those close to him, "Only today do I know that I may keep my head and be laid in the earth in peace.

sentences.zh: 」時人哀之。

translations.literal: ' People of the time pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who heard it were moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 有子道玄。

translations.literal: He had a son Daoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son named Daoxuan.
